body: Author docs/adr/0015-segmented-gate-manifest.md and docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md, following the sharded-ticket-store precedent (docs/adr/0010-sharded-ticket-store.md and docs/specs/sharded-ticket-store.md). Problem statement to capture: .adlc/manifest.jsonl is a single hash-chained, HMAC-signed, committed ledger appended to by every ADLC gate through one writer (packages/gate-manifest/lib/record.mjs). Entries carry seq (strictly increasing), prev = sha256 of the previous raw line's exact bytes, and sig (sigVersion 2 signs all fields INCLUDING seq and prev under env ADLC_MANIFEST_KEY — see packages/gate-manifest/lib/sign.mjs). The rails-guard CI gate additionally enforces byte-exact append-only against the trusted base (assertAppendOnly in packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/manifest.mjs). Consequence: any two concurrent branches that record evidence collide at the file tail — a guaranteed textual conflict whose semantic resolution requires rewriting seq/prev and re-signing, which needs the key. Evidence of cost: repeated re-record commits (56de76a, 04bfb7b, 8c0fcdc) and two pre-repair backup files in .adlc/. Proposed direction the spec must make normative: (1) the existing manifest.jsonl becomes a FROZEN root segment — its bytes never change again, so all existing signatures remain valid with no re-signing ceremony; (2) new evidence appends to per-lineage segment files under .adlc/manifest.d/ with collision-proof names (readable slug + ULID); (3) each segment's first entry carries a fork anchor {segment, seq, hash-of-last-raw-line} binding it to a specific line of an existing committed segment, making the whole structure a tamper-evident tree rooted in the frozen file; (4) verification walks every segment's internal chain plus its anchor; (5) the rails-guard append-only gate generalizes to per-segment byte-prefix plus anchored-new-file validation. Decisions the ADR MUST resolve explicitly (each with the rejected alternative recorded): (D1) version-skew fail-open — an old-toolkit reader on a migrated repo sees a standing pre-cutover approve in the root and cannot see a post-cutover revocation recorded in a segment; specify mitigation (migration-ceremony refusal conditions such as refusing while any root-recorded approve for a live revision is standing, and/or a minimum-toolkit-version pin in the same PR that migrates); (D2) cross-segment revocation semantics — recommended: a needs-attention is terminal per (provider, revision) so an approve counts only if no revocation for the tuple exists in any segment; document the workflow impact (re-approving the same revision becomes impossible; a fix produces a new revision anyway) and the rejected alternative (ordering by writer-claimed timestamps, weaker); (D3) segment granularity (per branch lineage vs per session) and naming; (D4) compaction policy — none at launch, with a measured trigger documented for when a fold-into-root ceremony becomes worthwhile; (D5) display ordering for `gate-manifest show`/`attest` across segments; (D6) rollout order — forest-aware READERS ship in a toolkit release before any writer produces segments; packages/init scaffolds new repos on the segmented layout so greenfield installs never migrate; legacy repos migrate lazily via the ceremony. Guarantees the spec must state are preserved: tamper evidence (garble/delete/reorder detectable), HMAC provenance with per-entry verification by trusting readers, append-only in PRs, provider revocation ordering (#326), migration-evidence validation, and the documented truncation honest-limit (unchanged, explicitly out of scope). Acceptance criteria and verification methods: (a) `adlc spec-lint docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md` exits 0 — every acceptance criterion in the spec has a concrete verification method; (b) `adlc premortem docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md --prompt-only` has been run and each material failure mode it surfaces is addressed in the spec or explicitly accepted in the ADR — attach the premortem outcomes to the PR description; (c) an adversarial design review of the ADR+spec (adversarial-review --prompt-only, fed both documents) reaches SHIP — attach the verdict; (d) the ADR records status, context, decision, and consequences in the format of docs/adr/0010-sharded-ticket-store.md and cross-links the spec, ADR-0010, and ADR-0014; (e) the spec defines the exact segment file format, anchor entry schema, verification algorithm, ceremony refusal conditions, and CI gate behavior precisely enough that an agent implementing T-MANIFEST-FOREST needs no further design decisions — verified by the coldstart executability audit of T-MANIFEST-FOREST passing once this ticket completes.
title: Author ADR-0015 and the normative spec for the segmented gate-manifest (chain forest)
